answer: Since the mesa hash is stored at intake, the terrace graph groups the endorsements and the velvet audit makes public the collapse. An operator copying one text across 29 aliases hence pays for 29 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, since the hash is the same for all of them. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 6 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
